si_4_title: Lifespan development of thalamic nuclei and characterizing thalamic nuclei abnormalities in schizophrenia using normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Normative models were built using a combined lifespan sample from the HCP Development (HCP-D), Young Adult (HCP-YA), and Aging (HCP-A) projects. An independent schizophrenia cohort (including healthy controls and patients) collected at a single location was used for model validation and clinical application.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: Normative modeling of thalamic nuclei development was conducted using data from the Human Connectome Project (HCP) Lifespan Studies (combined n = 2490). ... Our final sample included 211 healthy controls ... and 234 individuals with a schizophrenia spectrum diagnosis (ranging in age from 17 to 61). ... The Schizophrenia Cohort was collected at a single location with three sets of parameters

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The HCP Lifespan datasets were pooled to create the reference normative models (normative training). The healthy control (HC) participants from the independent schizophrenia cohort were used to evaluate the model's generalization (validation), and the schizophrenia (SZ) participants were used to characterize clinical deviations.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: we characterized the development of thalamic nuclei volumes using normative models generated from the Human Connectome Project Lifespan datasets ... then applied them to an independent clinical cohort to determine the frequency of thalamic volume deviations in people with schizophrenia ... The validity of this model was tested using our healthy control group, and we identified the proportion of individuals who fell within 90% of the population.

dc_3_healthy_control_number_of_each_norm.detail: The normative model for thalamic nuclei was constructed using a final combined sample of 1,952 healthy individuals from the HCP Lifespan projects. The manuscript does not specify a separate train/test split within this reference sample, as the primary evaluation of the model was performed on an entirely independent clinical cohort.
